chunks: From him, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Fadl al-Nawfali, from his father and his uncle together, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The one who is habitual in clipping his nails every Thursday, his eye will not suffer from conjunctivitis.

key_terms.أَدْمَنَ: He became habitual/customary in doing something

ai.seo_question: What is the benefit of clipping nails on Thursday according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the physical act of grooming to spiritual purity, reflecting the Shia emphasis on *fitrah* (natural disposition) and the holistic well-being of the believer. The specific mention of Thursday aligns with the prophetic tradition of preparing for Friday prayers, suggesting that maintaining cleanliness is an act of worship that enhances both physical health and spiritual readiness.

en.hubeali:
From him, from his father, from Abu Abdullah Bin Al Fazl Al Nowfaly, from his father, and his uncle, altogether, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who is habitual in taking his nails during every Thursday, would not have conjunctivitis of his eye’.
en.sarwar: 14. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from his father from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Fadl al-Nawfaliy from his father from his uncle all has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Whoever continues clipping his fingernails every Thursday will not experience eye ache.’”
